title: Exothermic and Endothermic Reactions
seo_title: Year 9 Science: Exothermic and Endothermic Reactions Worksheets (Energy Changes)
standard_text: Energy changes on changes of state (qualitative); exothermic and endothermic chemical reactions (qualitative); what catalysts do.
meta_desc: Free Year 9 science worksheets on exothermic and endothermic reactions: temperature changes, energy level diagrams, bond breaking and making, hand warmers and cold packs, and rates of reaction. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Breaking bonds takes in energy; making bonds gives it out.
body_html:
How to think about it

Every reaction transfers energy to or from the surroundings.

  • Exothermic: gives out energy, the temperature rises (burning, neutralisation, hand warmers).
  • Endothermic: takes in energy, the temperature falls (thermal decomposition, cold packs).
  • Breaking bonds takes in energy; making bonds gives it out. Higher temperature, concentration and surface area, and catalysts, speed reactions up.
Example

Start 20 °C, end 12 °C. Type?

Temperature fell

Answer: endothermic

Example

Start 19 °C, end 31 °C. Change?

31 − 19

Answer: 12 °C

Common mistakes

  • Thinking endothermic reactions get hotter.
  • Thinking breaking bonds releases energy.
  • Thinking a catalyst is used up.

faq.q: How can you tell if a reaction is exothermic?
faq.a: Measure the temperature before and after. If it rises, energy was transferred to the surroundings: the reaction is exothermic.

faq.q: What are some uses of endothermic reactions?
faq.a: Instant cold packs for sports injuries use an endothermic change, such as ammonium nitrate dissolving in water.

faq.q: What does an energy level diagram show?
faq.a: The energy of the reactants and products. If the products are lower, the reaction is exothermic; if higher, it is endothermic.
